definition: A Group 7 non-metal (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine) with 7 electrons in its outer shell, written X in family equations. The name means salt-forming.
msAccepts: a Group 7 non-metal with 7 outer-shell electrons
reactive non-metal that forms salts containing X⁻ ions
msAvoids: placing halogens among the metals
saying halogens are Group 17 with no mention of outer electrons

definition: Made of molecules containing exactly two atoms. The halogens exist as diatomic molecules — F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, I₂ — so astatine is predicted to form At₂ molecules too.
msAccepts: molecule made of two atoms (e.g. Cl₂)
exists as X₂ molecules
msAvoids: confusing with an ion made of two elements
saying it means 'two bonds'

definition: An ionic compound formed when a metal reacts with a halogen (or an acid). Halogen salts — NaCl, KBr, CaF₂, AgBr — all contain the halide ion X⁻.
msAccepts: ionic compound of a metal with a halogen, containing X⁻ ions
compound made when a metal replaces the hydrogen of an acid
msAvoids: calling covalent molecular HCl a salt
any compound with no ions

definition: The forces of attraction between separate molecules. Melting or boiling a molecular substance overcomes only these forces — no covalent bonds break.
msAccepts: forces of attraction between molecules, overcome on melting/boiling
weaker than covalent bonds; stronger down the halogen group as Mr rises
msAvoids: calling them covalent bonds between molecules
claiming covalent bonds break on melting

definition: A covalent molecular compound of hydrogen with a halogen, HX (HF, HCl, HBr, HI). All are acidic, poisonous gases that dissolve in water to give acidic solutions.
msAccepts: covalent HX gas that forms an acidic solution in water
e.g. hydrogen chloride gas dissolving to give hydrochloric acid
msAvoids: describing HX as ionic in the gas state
confusing the gas HCl with the solution HCl(aq)

definition: A ventilated enclosure that safely extracts poisonous gases. All halogen vapours are extremely poisonous, so halogen experiments are carried out inside one.
msAccepts: enclosure with extraction used for toxic vapours
why halogen demonstrations are done in one
msAvoids: calling it a safety screen or a hood that heats things
claiming it makes toxic gases safe to breathe

definition: A reaction in which a more reactive halogen pushes a less reactive halogen out of its salt solution, taking its place — chlorine displaces bromine from potassium bromide solution.
msAccepts: more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halogen from its halide solution
evidence for the decreasing reactivity down Group 7
msAvoids: saying the halogen displaces the metal's other partner 'bromide' element-style
reversing the direction (less reactive cannot displace more reactive)

definition: The negative ion of a halogen, X⁻ (F⁻, Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻). Formed when a halogen atom gains one electron; present in halogen salts and their aqueous solutions.
msAccepts: a halogen atom that has gained one electron, charge 1−
e.g. Cl⁻ in potassium chloride solution
msAvoids: confusing the ion Cl⁻ with the molecule Cl₂
wrong charge such as 2− or 1+

definition: An equation showing only the particles that actually change, written with their charges and state symbols; unchanging spectator ions are left out.
msAccepts: equation without spectator ions showing only reacting species with charges
e.g. Cl₂(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2Cl⁻(aq) + I₂(aq)
msAvoids: including the metal ion in a net ionic equation
omitting charges or state symbols

definition: An ion present in a reaction solution that does not take part — it is unchanged on both sides. K⁺ is the spectator ion in halogen displacement reactions.
msAccepts: ion that appears unchanged on both sides of the equation
K⁺ or Na⁺ during halogen displacement
msAvoids: claiming the metal ion is displaced
counting spectators among the reactants

definition: The substance that oxidises another by taking electrons away from it. It accepts electrons and is itself reduced. Chlorine oxidises bromide and iodide ions.
msAccepts: electron acceptor that is reduced itself
chlorine/bromine acting on halide ions in displacement reactions
msAvoids: saying the oxidising agent is oxidised
swapping the definitions with reducing agent

definition: The substance that reduces another by giving electrons to it. It gives away electrons and is itself oxidised. Halide ions act as reducing agents towards reactive halogens.
msAccepts: electron donor that is oxidised itself
bromide/iodide ions losing electrons to chlorine
msAvoids: saying the reducing agent is reduced
claiming metals are never reducing agents

definition: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen together: electrons are transferred, so one species loses them (oxidised) while another gains them (reduced).
msAccepts: simultaneous oxidation and reduction with electron transfer
halogen displacement described as redox
msAvoids: oxidation occurring without reduction
defining redox only by oxygen transfer
